Winter crate labels rules
New staff will learn how a new handler works

This page matters because mistakes with labels, crates, and animal notes can slow a flight and upset a traveler fast. At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps the handoff clean, calm, and traceable from check in to cabin loading. You are not just moving paperwork. You are protecting an animal, the passenger, and the cabin team all at once.

When a traveler arrives, read the crate label first and match it to the booking record before you touch anything else. Keep the name, route note, and animal details clear on the desk side so the next handoff does not stall. If a passenger looks nervous, stay steady and speak plainly. A worried traveler needs direct answers, not chatter. The senior coordinator should hear about any mismatch right away, because a small label problem can become a boarding delay in a hurry.

For bird travel, follow the crate guidance exactly as listed on the file and never guess from memory. <<FACT F071>> Hold to that instruction without adding extra notes on the label. For a large dog, the fee note must be checked before the file moves forward. <<FACT F057>> Do not promise anything until the record is confirmed and the payment line is clear.

Keep crate tags dry, legible, and attached where the cabin team can see them quickly. If a tag tears, replace it at once and update the desk copy. If the traveler brings extra gear, confirm that only approved items stay with the animal. Millie, and every other pet, must travel with the same careful attention to comfort and control.

During boarding, stay available for the cabin team and answer short questions fast. If something changes, send the update before the gate line moves on. We treat each journey as shared responsibility, and that means no loose ends, no shrugging, and no silent doubts. Remember to check, label, confirm, and speak up every single time.
